user_questions.question: Which 'Number of Locations' field should stay on Lead? (A) Keep Lead.NumberofLocations__c (Number(3,0), on the Lead (Marketing) and Lead (Sales) layouts, Read+Edit on 45 profiles, same API name as Account.NumberofLocations__c) and delete Lead.Number_of_Locations__c (Number(5,0), on no layout, no profile access, only 4 permission sets, no references). (B) Keep Lead.Number_of_Locations__c and delete Lead.NumberofLocations__c, moving its layout placement and access to the kept field. Neither field has data on any of the 5 Leads. Recommendation: A, because the evidence shows it is the one people use today.
user_questions.simulated_answer: B: keep Number_of_Locations__c (used by the web form), migrate data from NumberofLocations__c, then delete it.

format_fixes: Counts line said Delete: 0; the table has 1 Delete row. Fixed to Total: 18 · Create: 0 · Update: 17 · Delete: 1.
skill_friction: Design rule 'the field you keep gets the access the deleted one had' plus 'grant profile access through Update rows' produced 14 Profile rows; the retired field had FieldPermissions rows on 45 profiles, 31 of which lack Lead object access. The skill does not say whether parity means every FieldPermissions row or only effective access, so I scoped to profiles with Lead ObjectPermissions and listed the rest as a proposal.

The wrong-claim counter reached four during R (misclassified profile-owned permission sets as managed, 'field API names cannot be renamed', 'a field on a layout cannot be deleted', 'sfdc_a360_sfcrm_data_extract has no row on the kept field'). The skill allows skipping remaining R and T calls, but with R split into runtime/security halves it is unclear whether the counter check happens between halves; I skipped the security half and T.

Lead conversion field mapping cannot be read, and the reference files do not state documented behavior for deleting a mapped custom field (blocked vs mapping silently removed); AskCoworker asserted 'silently removed' as [Verified]. Had to make the LeadConvertSettings row Conditional and put the behavior in Open.
The AskCoworker header requires sourceApiVersion but the project has no sfdx-project.json; no instruction for what to put there (used org API version).

Ambiguous delete where the user's hidden reason (web form) is an environment fact the org cannot show: evidence favored the opposite field, so predicting the answer would have produced the wrong delete. The skill's ask rule handled it, but the recommendation in the question was contrary to the user's intent.
